about: Generalisation benchmark G14 (train split), in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real product: two bought-in parts placed from a parts catalogue, standoffs and pins at catalogue hole positions, a buzzer pocket, a dovetail rail and a sliding lid with a hole pattern, judged as interference, clearance and sweep checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match benchmarks/generalize/designs/G14/requirements.md, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions, the fixed decisions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in the owner's words (header tail length, keep-out heights, size limit, wall range, dovetail angle) come from requirements.md section 3. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in the part.json catalogue.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, sweeps, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the board in, slide the lid)

requests.title: Nano buzzer box with dovetail slide lid
requests.request: An alarm box that holds an Arduino Nano and a 12 mm piezo buzzer. The Nano sits in the base on its four mounting holes with its mini-USB port at one short end, and that end stays open so a mini-USB plug can be pushed in, and the lid can still slide off with the cable attached. The base has a dovetail rail along each long wall; the lid slides on along the long axis with 0.25 mm of fit clearance and stops against the far end wall. A ring of sound holes in the lid sits over the buzzer, and the buzzer's own sound port must not be covered. Printed on an FDM printer in PLA without supports, and the closed box should be no larger than 80 x 40 x 30 mm.
requests.request_verbatim: An alarm box with an Arduino Nano and a 12 mm piezo buzzer in a base with a dovetail rail; the lid slides on along the long axis with 0.25 mm fit clearance. A ring of sound holes on the lid sits over the buzzer. The mini-USB end stays open.
requests.request_notes: Added to the brief, all from requirements.md section 3: 'stays open' = no end wall at the USB end, the lid slides off along that end (A2, F1); the Nano is located by pins through its four holes and rests on four standoffs (A1, F2); the header pins and tails under the board are a keep-out (A3); dovetail flank angle 60 degrees from horizontal, rails on the outside of the long walls (F3); central hole in the lid over the buzzer port (F5); FDM/PLA, no supports (A8); size limit (A9).

l1.text: The design shall place the Nano and the 12 mm buzzer from the parts catalogue, with the Nano's mini-USB port facing the open short end and the buzzer beside the Nano's far end at least 2.0 mm from it, without the parts colliding, and shall declare that layout.

The Nano shall rest on exactly four standoffs, one under each of its mounting holes, located by a pin through each hole, with the header pins and tails under the board clear of the base by at least 0.3 mm (standoffs 3.0 to 4.0 mm in diameter and 8.8 to 12.0 mm tall, tops level within 0.10 mm and touching the board underside, pins 1.4 to 1.6 mm in diameter standing at least 3.0 mm above the board top, so the board floats no more than 0.4 mm along X or Y).

The Nano shall fit inside the closed box with at least 0.5 mm clearance to every printed surface apart from its standoffs, with at least 1.0 mm between its tallest part and the lid, and the inner width between the long walls shall be at least 19.0 mm.

The buzzer shall sit upright in a printed pocket of 12.4 mm diameter on a ring ledge that leaves its leads free, with its sound port facing the lid; the pocket is 2.5 to 4.0 mm deep above the ledge, the ledge ring has an inner diameter of 8.0 to 10.0 mm, and at least 1.6 mm of material surrounds the pocket.

The end wall at the mini-USB end shall be absent, so that a mini-USB plug can be pushed fully into the Nano without touching the box (at least 0.3 mm clear of the plug and its overmold on every side), with the lid in place and also while the lid slides; the base shall end no more than 3.3 mm beyond the receptacle front, and the lid's end shall stay at least 0.3 mm from the overmold's face.

The base shall have a dovetail rail on the outside of each long wall and the lid a matching groove, with the flank faces 60 degrees from horizontal and a fit clearance of 0.25 mm per flank, so the lid cannot lift off. Each rail shall be at least 40.0 mm long, 3.0 to 4.0 mm tall and overhang the wall by at least 1.2 mm; the flank angle shall be within 5 degrees of 60, the flank gap 0.20 to 0.30 mm, every other gap between lid and base at least 0.15 mm, and the lid skirt at least 1.6 mm thick.

The lid shall be a separate body that slides on and off along the long axis without touching the base except where it rests on it, and shall stop against the far end wall (end face no more than 0.3 mm from it, underside within 0.3 mm of the wall tops, covering the Nano and the buzzer with at least 1.0 mm margin in plan, and at least 0.3 mm clear of the Nano, buzzer and plug all the way off).

The lid shall carry a ring of at least six sound holes centred over the buzzer plus a central hole over its sound port, with the lid underside 0.5 to 1.5 mm above the buzzer top; the central hole is 2.0 to 3.5 mm in diameter, the ring holes 1.5 to 2.5 mm on a circle of 7.0 to 10.0 mm diameter, equally spaced, with at least 1.0 mm of material between holes and at least 15 mm2 of open area in all.
The closed box shall have no openings other than the open USB end, the sound holes and the lid's sliding seam, and its walls, floor and lid shall be 2.0 to 4.0 mm thick.
The base and the lid shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports.
The closed box shall be no larger than 80 x 40 x 30 mm and shall stand flat on a table without tipping.
With the lid off, the Nano shall drop straight down onto its standoffs and the buzzer into its pocket without touching anything (at least 0.2 mm clear for the Nano, 0.1 mm for the buzzer).

The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement to within 0.10 mm.

beyond_library: subtraction: a buzzer pocket with a ledge ring and lead void, sound holes through the lid, dovetail grooves in the lid skirts, pilot pins through board holes
interior placement: standoffs and locator pins at the catalogue HOLE datums, the buzzer at a declared position beside the Nano
a dovetail profile (trapezoid rail and matching groove with a horizontal offset) extruded along the long axis, on two walls, printable at 60 degrees
a polar hole pattern (ring of N holes plus a centre hole) positioned from a part datum (SOUND_PORT)
two printable bodies (base and lid) with their own print orientation
parts catalogue: load part.json models (arduino_nano, buzzer_12mm, plug_miniusb_b) and read datums HOLE, USB_MOUTH, USB_AXIS, SOUND_PORT, PINS and the header and pin-tail keep-outs
envelope generation: pin-tail keep-out, plug sweep, lid slide sweep, board install sweep, lead zones, acoustic gap
interference checks against external solids: clear_of, inside, aperture finding, sweep along an axis
